description: Streaming anomaly detection for multivariate and univariate data streams: 68 models, including LODA, HalfSpaceTrees, RSHash, xStream, OnlineKMeans, DenStream, DAMP, and SAND; conformal and SPOT calibration; drift monitoring; composable pipelines; prequential evaluation; pysad-live CLI; pysad-mcp server with auto-discovered tools and parameter metadata; labeled SMAP, MSL, and SMD datasets; optional PyO3 kernels.
rules: Use fit_partial(x), score_partial(x), and fit_score_partial(x) on 1-D arrays of shape (num_features,). Decision-capable models and pipelines also expose predict_partial(x), fit_predict_partial(x), predict(X), and fit_predict(X) returning 0 or 1.
Higher scores always mean more anomalous instances across every detector, postprocessor, ensembler, and calibrator.
score_partial(x) never mutates model state; use fit_score_partial(x) for prequential score-before-learn evaluation.
Univariate detectors expect a 1-D array of shape (1,), such as np.array([value]), not a scalar or shape (1, 1); reshape 1-D series with values.reshape(-1, 1) for ArrayStreamer.
Compose streaming pipelines with | (StreamPipeline, e.g. StandardScaler() | LODA() | ConformalProbabilityCalibrator()) and ensemble detectors with & (ModelEnsemble).

Convert arbitrary raw scores into [0, 1] alert scales using ConformalProbabilityCalibrator, SPOTProbabilityCalibrator, or GaussianTailProbabilityCalibrator, paired with ThresholdFilter or QuantileFilter.
Evaluate labeled streams prequentially with pysad.evaluation.evaluate_stream and streaming metrics such as AUROCMetric, AUPRMetric, PrecisionMetric, RecallMetric, RollingMetric, and WindowedMetric.
Import public classes from their subpackages (pysad.models, pysad.integrations, pysad.utils, pysad.evaluation, pysad.statistics, pysad.transform.*) rather than private module paths.
Use LODA.explain_partial(x), HalfSpaceTrees.explain_partial(x), or KitNet.explain_partial(x) to attribute per-feature contributions to an anomaly score.

Run PyOD batch models on streams with ReferenceWindowModel or OneFitModel, embed PySAD detectors in River or scikit-learn with PySADToRiverAdapter or PySADToScikitLearnAdapter, and score River forecasters with PredictiveAnomalyDetector.
Run live streaming anomaly detection with the pysad-live CLI, for example: pysad-live --source synthetic --detector loda --calibrator conformal.
Supported sources are synthetic, nyc_taxi, arrhythmia, creditcard, or a path to a CSV file; use --csv-delimiter and --no-csv-header for custom CSV files, and --max-points to limit the stream.
Choose a detector (loda, half_space_trees, rs_hash, lof, rrcf, knncad, smart_sifter, seasonal_esd, xstream, mad) and calibrator (conformal, spot, gaussian_tail, anomaly_likelihood, group_conformal).

Tune the run with --detector-seed, --detector-kwargs, --calibrator-window, --calibrator-kwargs, and --threshold; adjust the terminal with --width, --height, --history, --refresh-rate, --max-features, --no-labels, and --no-ribbon.
Open the web dashboard with --web --port 8080 --host 127.0.0.1, or run headless JSON output with --json-output and log alerts to a file with --log-file.

Install pysad[mcp] and run pysad-mcp. The server auto-discovers tools from pysad.models.__all__ and pysad.statistics.__all__. Each discovered tool is named pysad_<lowercase_name> and lists constructor parameters and defaults in its metadata.

Install the optional PyO3 extension separately with pip install pysad_kernels. HalfSpaceTrees and RobustRandomCutForest use available tree kernels automatically. LODA and StreamKMPlusPlus need use_rust=True.
If a kernel is unavailable, the detector uses NumPy. Floating-point rounding can change StreamKMPlusPlus cluster assignments.
